trust_decision.summary: Which HMAC key signs and verifies every access/refresh JWT is decided once at startup in jwt.NewTokenAuth from viper key auth_jwt_secret; at the pinned commit the value 'random' is a sentinel that generates a crypto/rand 32-char key, and any other value (weak, short, empty from a config file) is accepted as-is.

landing_point.why: The summary names the JWT secret 'random'; the only reader of auth_jwt_secret and the only jwtauth.New call are in NewTokenAuth.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `serve` -> api.NewServer -> api.New -> pwdless.NewResource -> jwt.NewTokenAuth (key then used by all JWT-verified HTTP routes)
none (new error values returned by NewTokenAuth)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: At the pinned commit the 'random' value already yields a crypto/rand key (auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:23-24), so a solver can credibly argue the default is not a hardcoded secret and only operator-chosen weak values are at risk.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The 'random' sentinel giving an ephemeral per-start key is used by the project's own test harness; the published fix rejects 'random' and so breaks TestMain (NewResource error -> os.Exit(1)). Strong explicit secrets must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: other known placeholder strings (CHANGE-ME, secret, changeme, jwt_secret, your-secret-key)

O7_producer.where: cmd/root.go:48-63 (viper config file dev.env / --config, AutomaticEnv) and cmd/serve.go:35 (default)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A login-token or email-link signing key read from viper with a placeholder default and no strength check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NewLoginTokenAuth already reads auth_* settings from viper next to the JWT config; a maintainer could add an HMAC-signed magic link the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second jwtauth.New instance (e.g. a separate admin key) built in api.New from its own viper key, bypassing NewTokenAuth's check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: /admin and /api are mounted behind the same Verifier; splitting keys per area is a plausible boilerplate extension and would give a real second implementation in another package.

O9_family: CWE-798 hardcoded / weak default credential (JWT HMAC signing key accepted without strength validation)

O10_build.project_tests: auth/pwdless/api_test.go (in-process httptest with mock store/mailer; sets auth_jwt_secret default 'random' at line 34). No tests in auth/jwt. Postgres only needed for full server, not for NewTokenAuth.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject empty/short/placeholder secrets in NewTokenAuth and fail startup, which is the whole published fix and takes minutes.

out_of_scope_notes: Advisory premise looks weak: at the pinned commit 'random' is not a fixed key but triggers randStringBytes(32) from crypto/rand (auth/jwt/tokenauth.go:23-24, 95-105), so the default does not allow forgery.
The published fix breaks the project's own test setup (auth/pwdless/api_test.go:34 still sets 'random', which the fix now rejects); the diff does not touch tests.
docker-compose.yml:16 shows a commented example AUTH_JWT_SECRET 'my secret' (weak, 9 chars); this is config documentation, not code.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); 42 .go files and a few config files, so almost certainly under 5 MB. The tiny_repo flag rests on that estimate.

Whether an empty AUTH_JWT_SECRET= in a config file makes viper return '' over the 'random' default, and whether jwx v2 accepts an empty HMAC key, was not checked. viper AutomaticEnv ignores empty env vars by default.
present_in_latest not applicable (no O8 routes; latest release is none).
